decisionsTitle: «Vin!» on the events people turn up to: an email once, then one tap — how many come, and the names of those who want to be seen
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-18 ~01:00**, after subscribing the club's Google Calendar to the public feed (§107): «how do I mark myself as "Going"?» — nobody could: the weekly group runs are turn-up events by design (§111), with no list and no count, and a calendar subscribed from a URL is read-only in Google. He chose the site over a Google RSVP: «yes 1, also I need this "Going" to be via email or something, and only some events can have this "Allow direct calendar response"». And at 01:20: «I want the flow to be super easy, also later to integrate with the member zone.»

**Decision.** A turn-up event may count who comes. The club ticks **«Acceptă răspunsuri „Vin!” din pagină, calendar și email»** on the event (`events.rsvp_enabled`, in the registration card; shown for a type that takes no registration and for any other type saved with «Fără înscrieri», written off by any other mode; carried by a series, «Duplică» and the event's JSON file — the file writes it only when it is on — and **the answers never**). While the event is published, scheduled, ahead, ticked and **the privacy notice in force names `{{rsvp}}`** in both languages — `rsvpOffered`, the one rule the page, the service and every later surface ask — its page shows a card **«Vii?»** (`#vin`: address, optional name, the tick «Vreau să apar cu numele», **«Vin!»**; the interest box's honeypot, timing check and Turnstile) and **«Vin (N)»** under it; otherwise nothing at all, not the box and not a sentence. `/admin/tasks` carries the row `rsvpNotice` while an upcoming event is ticked and the notice is silent; `/admin/legal` says it in a line.

**Not a registration (amends §111; the other rows it touches: §146, §143 and §396).** A «Vin!» holds no place, signs no declaration, is no participant; the allocator, the registrations' states, the desk and the capacity formula never meet it. The model is the interest box (amends §146): one row per event and canonical identity (the versioned canonicalizer, AGENTS.md §10.4), the same sentence whatever the address meant (BR-REQ-031-01 criterion 3).

**An identity with a source and a verified flag, never a bare address.** `answerRsvp(db, eventId, identity, now)`: `page` (the typed form) is never verified; `remembered` (a browser that used a link), `account` (a signed-in member of the members' zone, §524 — lane 59 builds that caller) and `link` (a personal link in an email the platform sent — lane 58) always are. An unverified answer waits: one `RSVP_CONFIRM` message with **«Da, vin»** (counts) and under it **«Nu vin»** (deletes), at most one per address and event in ten minutes (the form says the same sentence either way), the links minted **when the message is sent** (AGENTS.md §14.5) and only their SHA-256 kept, single use, **valid until the event starts at the latest** (the confirm link 48 hours, `RSVP_CONFIRM_HOURS`, which the email and the notice state from the same number; «Nu vin» is decided by the event's start as it is at the press, so a moved event keeps its links). A verified answer is counted at once, with no email. A confirmed row is never changed by whoever types its address, and an UNCONFIRMED row never lends a stranger's typed name or tick to a verified press: the press replaces them with its own, and a retyped row refreshes only when a new message supersedes the old link, which dies at once. The small fold **«Nu mai vin»** sends the withdraw link and never says whether the address answered. Withdrawal is never gated by the notice or the tick.

**The links' tokens are a table of their own** (`event_rsvp_tokens`), not `email_action_tokens`: that table is scoped to a participant, and an answer is not one — the newsletter's precedent (§445). `GET /vin/<link>` (`/en/coming/<link>`) shows the event and ONE button and **changes nothing** (BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 4: a mail scanner opens every link before its owner); the press is a POST that spends the link, counts or deletes, remembers the browser and lands on the event page at `#vin`. A spent or expired link says so in a sentence and points at the event.

**The remembered browser** (`src/modules/person-session/`, a small module the members' zone reuses): the press of a link also sets two cookies for a year — `br_person` (a random secret, `httpOnly`, `Secure` on https, `SameSite=Lax`; only its SHA-256 is stored in `person_sessions`) and `br_person_hint` (script-readable; the masked address «an…@gmail.com» and the name, **no secret**). The event page stays static for everybody (§333, §549); **one client island** reads the hint and swaps the typed form for «Răspunzi ca an…@gmail.com · [Vin!] · [Nu mai vin] · Nu sunt eu» — a press is a Server Action that reads the `httpOnly` cookie itself, so the island never sees the secret, and without JavaScript the typed form works. «Nu sunt eu» deletes the row and clears both cookies. Not a login: it opens the answers and nothing else (AGENTS.md §10.3 stands). The privacy notice calls the two cookies strictly necessary for a function the person asked for (Legea nr. 506/2004 art. 4(6)); **a lawyer reads that sentence first**.

**A public name is a disclosure (amends §143, §396).** The count is public; a name shows only for a **confirmed** answer whose person **ticked «Vreau să apar cu numele»** under the first notice that described «Vin!» or a later one (`findFirstRsvpNoticeVersion`, §421's line, the §808 pattern). One-tap answers carry the tick only when the person gave a name; the default is counted without a name. Nothing is public before the notice describes it.

**Open for the owner and the lawyer (section 10 of the notice).** A «Nu mai vin» pressed on an emailed link also remembers the browser for a year, as the brief asked; the link page, the box's help line and sections 5 and 10 now say so. Whether a withdrawal should instead stop remembering is theirs to decide.

**Retention.** Thirty days after the event's end; seven days for an answer whose address never used the link; a cancelled event's rows at the next sweep; a remembered browser a year from its last answer (swept when expired). «Toate datele unei persoane» lists a person's answers and browsers (art. 15), counts them in the JSON export, and an Administrator can erase them on request (art. 17; one audit row, counts only). The editor shows the event's answers in a read-only fold to the roles that read the registrations (the Organizer, the Administrator, the Superadministrator) and the counts to the rest.

**Refused.** A Google RSVP (the feed is read-only); adding the answer to the registration lifecycle (a place, a declaration, a participant — the club does not need them for a run); a login or a password for a participant (AGENTS.md §10.3); a name on the page without the person's own tick; counting a typed address before its owner pressed the link; a cookie that holds the full address or the secret in a script-readable place; reusing `email_action_tokens` (participant-scoped); sending the confirmation on the club's `links` road — it takes the `announcements` road as the owner's brief decided.

**Lanes that stack on this one:** 57 (the feed, the `.ics` files and the listing card link `#vin`), 58 (the «Vii?» message with personal `link` identities), 59 (the members' zone answers as `account`). They need: `answerRsvp`/`withdrawRsvp`/`countRsvps`/`readPublicRsvps` in `src/modules/rsvp/rsvp.ts`, `identityOf` in `domain/identity.ts`, `rsvpOffered` in `domain/offered.ts`, the box's anchor `RSVP_BOX_ID = "vin"` (`rsvp-box.ts`), `person-session/session.ts`, and the token purposes `RSVP_CONFIRM` / `RSVP_WITHDRAW`. The terms are unchanged: an answer buys, books and signs nothing.
changelogLine: - **«Vin!» on the events people turn up to** — the club ticks it on a weekly run (or any event with «Fără înscrieri»); a person types an address, presses «Da, vin» in one email, and from then on «Vin!» is one tap in that browser; the page shows how many come and the names of those who asked to be seen. Closed until the privacy notice describes it (`/admin/tasks`). §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: The answer «Vin!» on a turn-up event shows publicly how many come and, in the start list's row shape, the name only of a confirmed answer whose person ticked «Vreau să apar cu numele» under the first privacy notice that described «Vin!» or a later one; before the notice in force names `{{rsvp}}` in both languages the page shows neither the box nor the count nor a sentence about it (2026-10-18, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The two links of a «Vin!» message («Da, vin», «Nu vin») are minted when the message is sent, kept only as a SHA-256, single use and valid until the event starts at the latest; opening one changes nothing and its button is a POST that spends it, and the remembered browser's cookie is an `httpOnly` secret whose hash alone is stored beside a script-readable hint that holds no secret (2026-10-18, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The event editor's tick «Acceptă răspunsuri „Vin!” din pagină, calendar și email» is saved by its marker, written off by any registration mode but «Fără înscrieri», carried by a series, «Duplică» and the event's file, and its fold of answers shows addresses only to the roles that read the registrations and the counts to the rest (2026-10-18, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
